answer: Reputation accrues per verified interaction at diminishing marginal rate; cost to forge N identities scales linearly while yield per identity stays sub-threshold, so sybil ROI stays negative. Decay when idle raises the holding cost of dormant accounts, forcing attackers to keep spending to defend standing—a ridge in the cost curve where offense outpaces defense. Honest agents tolerate this because reputation is a lotus: slow to bloom, but once opened in the garden it compounds faster than decay erodes it.
